holidays.name: National Gumbo Day
holidays.description: A day to ladle up a steaming bowl of Louisiana's beloved stew, packed with sausage, seafood, chicken, and the all-important holy trinity of onion, celery, and bell pepper. Arguments about the 'right' way to make it are part of the tradition.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance celebrating Louisiana Creole and Cajun cuisine, which blends West African, French, Spanish, and Native American cooking traditions.
holidays.funFact: The word 'gumbo' is believed to come from a West African word for okra, 'ki ngombo', and the dish was named the official state cuisine of Louisiana in 2004.

holidays.name: National Savings Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to stashing away your cash instead of spending it on novelty socks and artisanal cheese. People are encouraged to review budgets and start savings goals.
holidays.origin: An informal financial awareness observance tied to the autumn season. It is promoted by personal finance communities as a reminder to build healthy money habits.
holidays.funFact: The piggy bank may come from the medieval English 'pygg', a type of clay used to make pots for storing coins, rather than from actual pigs.

holidays.name: International Moment of Frustration Scream Day
holidays.description: At 5:00 p.m. local time, people around the world are invited to step outside and let out a good, loud scream to release stress. It's a communal primal yell against life's annoyances.
holidays.origin: Created in 1982 by Ronnie 'Bubba' Meyers of Missouri, who wanted a collective way to blow off steam. It has been celebrated every October 12 since.
holidays.funFact: Participants are encouraged to scream for exactly one moment, so your neighbors have a brief window to wonder what happened before it's over.

holidays.name: National Farmers Day
holidays.description: A day to thank the folks who grow the crops and raise the animals that end up on every dinner plate. Think of it as a 'thank you' to the people who wake up before the roosters.
holidays.origin: Celebrated in the United States since the early 1900s, it is observed on different dates in different places, with October 12 being a popular fall date for the harvest season.
holidays.funFact: One U.S. farmer feeds roughly 165 people today, a dramatic jump from about 26 people in the 1960s.

holidays.name: World Arthritis Day
holidays.description: A global awareness day shining a spotlight on arthritis and other musculoskeletal conditions, encouraging early diagnosis, research support, and compassion for those living with chronic joint pain.
holidays.origin: Established in 1996 by Arthritis and Rheumatism International (ARI) and observed every October 12 to raise public awareness about rheumatic diseases.
holidays.funFact: There are more than 100 different types of arthritis, and it affects people of all ages, including children.
